title: SR 1 over Six Mile Creek | schematic with assumed supports
source_note: 2026 thin-overlay drawing envelope plus 2025 NBI and explicitly hypothetical structural support geometry.
assumptions: This is a schematic overlay-plan reconstruction with a deliberately hypothetical structural scaffold; it is not a detailed as-built model.
2025 NBI item 43A=2 and 43B=01 identify continuous concrete slab, not concrete beams. The earlier research candidate type was corrected.
Source p.4 incorrectly repeats structure 001-90-00230-B (Wabash). The cover identifies 001-90-07052-B, NBI 000370 and Six Mile Creek consistently; the cover identity is retained.
Source p.4 overall 72 ft 7.25 in governs; p.7 labels a schematic 72 ft overlay length. NBI 22.2 m overall and 8.5 m maximum span are rounded inventory values.
All supports, foundation envelopes and slab thickness are hypothetical. Original substructure geometry has not been established.
Native X station, Y transverse and Z up. The 6 m local elevation, level longitudinal grade and skew direction are assumed; NBI gives skew magnitude only.
No internal reinforcement, pile tips, traffic, observed defects or drainage details are invented.

detail_coverage.detail: Deck length/width, clear roadway, crossfall and nominal replacement overlay are sourced. Approach edge lengths come from a not-to-scale schematic. The deck overlay covers the 44 ft roadway between the barrier toes and stops at the joint-seal envelopes; the approach polymer overlay is recorded in the approach notes, not modelled (thickness not given). Approach far ends are square to S.R. 1, with the 20.5/36.5 ft lengths on the 44 ft roadway edges (sheet 7 plan).

450 mm structural slab, symmetric 6.664875 / 8.5 / 6.664875 m support spans, 150 mm end overhangs, wall piers, end walls and foundations are illustrative. NBI supplies three spans, continuous concrete slab type and 20-degree skew, not these details.
General barrier envelope only. Height, tapered section and rail joints are assumed.
No original slab reinforcement, verified support section/positions, foundations, drainage, construction joints or exact rail details were obtained.

values.barrier move: rigid, 30.95 mm outward along the skewed end lines and down the 1.56 % crossfall
values.deck overlay ends: stopped 15 mm short of each joint centre line, at the edge of the 30 mm seal envelope (seal top was 8.5 mm inside the overlay)
values.approach polymer overlay (sheets 3, 7, 8: 44 ft wide, 279 SYS for both; recorded, not modelled

known_deviations.deviation: The non-warranted polymer overlay on both RCBAs (44 ft roadway, 279 SYS for both) is recorded in the approach notes and dimensions only; it is not shown as a layer or as a separate finish on the approach top faces.
known_deviations.reason: No sheet gives its thickness, and each part is one closed solid shown in one manifest colour (the viewer ignores vertex colours and needs one mesh per part), so a face-level finish would need a new part of invented thickness.

known_deviations.deviation: Each 30 mm seal envelope spans the full 47 ft 1 1/2 in deck (Y = +/-7.18185 m, 50.15 ft along the skew) and passes under the barrier ends; sheet 7 dimensions each joint 47 ft along the skew across the 44 ft roadway hatch (44 ft / cos 20 deg = 46.8 ft) and sheet 8 gives 94 lft for both.
known_deviations.reason: Minor item of the second review, outside the scope of revision 1.2; trimming each seal to |Y| <= 6.7056 m is left for a later correction.
